function: Excluded, above_phy (p. 4, p. 6): the learned part, k-medoids clustering with Silhouette analysis, groups users and assigns subcarriers and time slots (scheduling); transmit power comes from convex optimization with water-filling (p. 5).
notes: Title and DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2024.3394041 on p. 1 (IEEE IoT J 11(18), 2024), so the PDF is this work. It is a research article that proposes and simulates a method, so source_type and survey do not apply. The only learning is k-medoids clustering of the users' channel gains with Silhouette analysis to set the number of users per subcarrier, which the paper calls ML and unsupervised learning (p. 1, abstract and index terms; p. 4: "A subcarrier is assigned to an optimum number of users such that the interference between the users is minimized using a machine learning (ML) strategy"; p. 6, Algorithm 1: "Step 1: ML-Based Clustering", "Step 2: Sub-carrier Allocation"). Counted as a learned component, it decides user grouping and the subcarrier and time-slot assignment of a terrestrial single-cell uplink, that is scheduling, which is above the physical layer. The physical-layer decision, transmit power, is solved by convex optimization with KKT conditions and iterative water-filling (p. 5: "The power can be allocated to the different users using the water-filling algorithm"; p. 6, Algorithm 1, Step 3), so no physical-layer decision is learned jointly. For the reviewer: (a) the clustering runs on each channel realization without any training (p. 5: "without any training on a data set"); if it is not counted as a learned component, the first code is no_learning instead. (b) function would also apply: despite ISAC in the title, the system model, the problem, and the results contain no sensing (pp. 3-4; the objective and the only metric are the aggregated uplink EMF exposure, Figs. 4-7, pp. 6-7), and the method solves none of the seven problems. (c) system would also apply: N single-antenna UPWDs (p. 3), a scalar received signal at the BS (eq. 1, p. 3), and backscatter tags with a fixed reflection coefficient (Table I, p. 6) rather than a RIS. Results exist: MATLAB Monte Carlo simulations with Rayleigh fading and the path loss of [30] (p. 6), against the OFDMA scheme of [23] and the ML-based PD-NOMA scheme of [24], both without backscatter (p. 6).
